name: Windows Command Shell
description:
Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution. The Windows command shell (cmd) is the primary command prompt on Windows systems which is used in industrial control system environments. The Windows command prompt can be used to control almost any aspect of a system, with various permission levels required for different subsets of commands. The command prompt can be invoked remotely via  [Remote Services](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T0886) (e.g., Telnet, SSH, RDP, etc.) 

Batch files (ex: .bat or .cmd) also provide the shell with a list of sequential commands to run, as well as normal scripting operations such as conditionals and loops. Common uses of batch files include long or repetitive tasks, or the need to run the same set of commands on multiple systems. 

Adversaries may leverage [cmd](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0106) to execute various commands and payloads. Common uses include [cmd](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0106) to execute a single command, or abusing [cmd](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0106) interactively with input and output forwarded over a command and control channel. 

Within industrial control system networks, adversaries may abuse the use of Windows Command Shell on overlap assets that run on Microsoft Windows operating systems (Workstations, Data Historians, Human Machine Interfaces, Application Servers, Jump Hosts, etc.).

telemetry.name: Process Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a process with executable, command line, parent and security context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

configuration_example.label: Sysmon filter fragment · merge into the reviewed lab configuration
configuration_example.note: This fragment only selects the named process. It is not a complete production policy. Inspect the installed schema with sysmon64 -s; preserve existing rules, then apply the reviewed complete configuration with sysmon64 -c <configuration-file>.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

sources.title: Apple Endpoint Security framework for macOS

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Windows Command Shell Execution in ICS

analytics.name: Analytic 2087
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies cmd.exe or .bat/.cmd execution from an unexpected parent or user context, execution from transient/user-writable paths, suspicious command chaining, or shell activity followed by OT-relevant discovery, credential, remote-access, or configuration behavior. Alert only when the interpreter is not part of the asset's approved software/automation baseline or its execution context violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/user rule, and require OT-relevant corroboration such as access to engineering files, ICS software/API use, communications with protected OT assets, configuration change, or another suspicious follow-on behavior. Suppress documented vendor software, engineering workflows, diagnostics, backup, patching, and approved maintenance.

tuning.description: Approved vendor applications/services that legitimately spawn cmd.exe
Chaining, discovery, remote execution, file transfer, or ICS tool/API invocation

software.name: Stuxnet
software.description: [Stuxnet](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0603) will store and execute SQL code that will extract and execute Stuxnet from the saved CAB file using xp_cmdshell with the following command: `set @s = master..xp _ cmdshell extrac32 /y +@t+ +@t+x; exec(@s);` (Citation: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien February 2011)

references.source_name: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien February 2011
references.description: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien 2011, February W32.Stuxnet Dossier (Version 1.4) Retrieved November 17, 2024.

software.name: Industroyer
software.description: The name of the [Industroyer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0604) payload DLL is supplied by the attackers via a command line parameter supplied in one of the main backdoors that executes shell commands. (Citation: Anton Cherepanov, ESET June 2017)

references.description: Anton Cherepanov, ESET 2017, June 12 Win32/Industroyer: A new threat for industrial control systems Retrieved. 2017/09/15

actors.name: Sandworm Team
actors.description: [Sandworm Team](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0034) uses the MS-SQL server xp_cmdshell command, and PowerShell to execute commands. (Citation: Dragos October 2018)

references.description: Dragos 2018, October 12 Anatomy of an Attack: Detecting and Defeating CRASHOVERRIDE Retrieved. 2019/10/14

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Restrict cmd.exe, batch files, and command-shell child processes to approved binaries, paths, parent processes, accounts, and maintenance workflows on Windows-based ICS assets. Preserve documented vendor and engineering dependencies.

simulation.prerequisites: Use a process simulator or isolated test rig with no connection to production controllers or physical actuators. Preserve safety interlocks; destructive effects require synthetic evidence, not real equipment damage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
